text:
Jordan Li: FYI running into "RuntimeError: Event loop is closed" when using the async Python SDK inside a Jupyter notebook. Repro is trivial:

```python
# notebook cell 1
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient(api_key="x")  # created at import/top-level

# notebook cell 2
await client.embed("hello")
# later: restart kernel / shutdown -> traceback on exit
```

Traceback shows the error coming from teardown: something trying to call asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete(...) during interpreter shutdown. Happens on Python 3.11.4, httpx 0.24.1, sdk 0.9.2. Anyone seen this pattern?

Priya Nair: yep, we've had reports from FastAPI users too when they put a client at module level. Our libs used to register an atexit handler to auto-close a global client and that can call run_until_complete which is unsafe when another loop (pytest/jupyter/uvicorn) owns the loop. Bad combo.

Ben S.: can you check if the client implements __aenter__/__aexit__? best pattern is to use an app lifespan hook or an async context manager. Also double-check client.aclose() is awaited before kernel shutdown.

Jordan Li: it does have async context manager, but this is an accidental pattern (top-level client for convenience in notebooks). Reproducer stack (trimmed):
```
File "/usr/lib/python3.11/atexit.py", line 34, in _run_exitfuncs
  func()
File "/opt/.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood/sdk.py", line 512, in _atexit_close
  loop.run_until_complete(self.aclose())
RuntimeError: Event loop is closed
```

Priya Nair: exact problem. Two things we should do: 1) remove blocking run_until_complete() from atexit handlers; 2) make __del__ / finalizers safe without blocking the loop. We can use weakref.finalize to run a non-blocking warning instead of attempting to run async cleanup during interpreter teardown.

Ben S.: agree. Implementation idea: a) make client.aclose() idempotent and safe to call multiple times; b) in __del__ / finalize, do: try: loop = asyncio.get_running_loop(); loop.call_soon_threadsafe(asyncio.create_task, self.aclose()) except RuntimeError: logger.warning("AsyncClient destroyed outside running loop; call client.aclose() to cleanup")

Jordan Li: that approach avoids run_until_complete but note: asyncio.get_running_loop() raises if no loop, so fallback to warning is fine. For notebooks the kernel may be shutting down so neither will work; so warn is best.

Priya Nair: also a typing/typing-stubs nit: our AsyncClient stub in py.typed doesn't expose __aenter__/__aexit__ types so linters complain when people use `async with AsyncClient() as c:`. Add proper AsyncContextManager return types in stubs.

Ben S.: +1. Also add docs showing recommended patterns for three runtimes: notebooks, pytest-asyncio tests, and fastapi/uvicorn apps (use lifespan event close). Example snippet for FastAPI:
```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from redwood import AsyncClient

app = FastAPI()
client = AsyncClient(api_key=...)  # single instance per process

@app.on_event("shutdown")
async def shutdown():
    await client.aclose()
```

Jordan Li: can we also add a small unit test in CI that simulates pytest-asyncio teardown so we don't regress? Something that creates client, awaits acall, then uses atexit simulation to ensure no run_until_complete is invoked.

Priya Nair: good call. I'll add a test and a CHANGELOG entry. Also we should surface a migration note: "If you depended on SDK auto-close at process exit, please call client.aclose() explicitly or use async with; implicit close on interpreter shutdown is not guaranteed."

CI Bot: Issue #2390 created: "python-async: avoid run_until_complete in atexit/finalizers; improve async cleanup and typing" (labels: sdk, bug, docs)

Ben S.: I'll draft the PR removing the atexit register and adding weakref.finalize + warning + typing stubs. Assigning to @ben_s.

Jordan Li: thanks folks — saved my notebook session :) :thumbsup:
